q: What is the minimum floor area of the birthing room?
n: Birthing room: at least 10.50 m² with a least dimension of 3.00 m. Remember this: birthing room "10.5 and 3" (10.50 sq. m., least side 3.00 m). Doors "0.90 to 1.20". Window sill 1.60 m high for privacy. Placenta pit bottom 1.50 m above groundwater.

q: What is the least dimension of the birthing room?
If the waiting area is placed along a corridor, the corridor width must not go below:
n: Corridor waiting is allowed if the corridor stays at least 1.10 m wide.

q: What is the minimum clear opening of the main door of a birthing home?
n: Main door: minimum 0.90 m, maximum 1.20 m.

q: What door combination is described as most functional for the birthing room and ward?
o: 0.80 m + 0.40 m leaves, 1.20 m clear when fully open

q: If the delivery room has windows, how high must the sill be above the finished floor?
n: 1.60 m sill keeps privacy while allowing light and cross ventilation.

q: Up to what ward capacity can the toilet and bath be a common facility for staff and patients?
n: Below 6 beds one shared T&B; more beds need more toilets.

q: Where must the scrub-up area of a birthing home be located?
o: Outside the birthing room, away from main traffic
n: Recessed wall or open space outside the birthing room.

q: How must the interior walls of the birthing room meet the floor?
o: Concave at the base for a seamless finish
n: Coved base prevents dirt and dust from collecting.

q: If a placenta pit is built, its bottom must be at least how far above the groundwater level?
n: Pit bottom ≥ 1.50 m above groundwater; not in flood-prone areas; authorized access only.

q: What supplementary requirement keeps a birthing home able to handle deliveries during a power outage?
o: A portable generator or battery-operated light source
n: Light must stay on for delivery even when power is cut.

q: Why does the birthing home guideline require ramps to follow BP 344?
o: BP 344 considers pregnant women as persons with disability
n: Pregnant women are treated as PWD under the Accessibility Law.

q: A designer proposes a birthing room of 2.80 m × 4.00 m. Does it comply?
o: Yes, the area is above 10.50 sq. m.
No, the least dimension is below 3.00 m
No, the area is below 12.00 sq. m.
n: 2.80 × 4.00 = 11.20 m² passes the area but fails the 3.00 m least dimension.

q: True or false: The birthing room must have a minimum floor area of 10.50 sq. m.
n: 10.5 and 3. Remember this: birthing room "10.5 and 3" (10.50 sq. m., least side 3.00 m). Doors "0.90 to 1.20". Window sill 1.60 m high for privacy. Placenta pit bottom 1.50 m above groundwater.

q: Fill in the blank: Birthing home main door clear opening = minimum 0.90 m, maximum ___ m.

n: Sill high enough to block the view in.

q: True or false: A placenta pit may be located in a flood-prone area if it is lined with concrete.
